plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a hybrid thickness initialization scheme (60% QWOT±10% perturbation, 40% harmonic half/double multiples with ±5nm noise injection) improves convergence for a HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack compared to pure QWOT-centered initialization. Drawn from recalled knowledge that quarter-wave optical thickness stacks form the standard basis for dichroic filters, but that symmetric initialization can trap gradient descent in local minima. The harmonic perturbation hypothesis is that breaking thickness symmetry helps the optimizer discover non-obvious layer combinations that still satisfy the dual-band spectral requirements.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 Dichroic Stack with Hybrid Thickness Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A hybrid initialization scheme combining 60% QWOT-centered candidates with 40% harmonic half/double-multiple thickness candidates, plus ±5nm noise injection in the first optimization step, will produce higher best_target_score and maintain tightest_margin compared to pure QWOT±10% initialization across iteration rounds.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) stacks create constructive interference for reflection at design wavelengths. For a dichroic filter blocking 400-700nm while passing 1530-1565nm, the high-index HfO2 and low-index SiO2 layers should have optical thicknesses near λ/4 at a center wavelength in the visible blocking band. However, pure QWOT initialization creates symmetry that can trap gradient-based optimizers; harmonic perturbations (λ/8, λ/2 multiples) break this symmetry while remaining physically meaningful.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer stack starting from air: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, terminated on fused silica substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
Initialization scheme: 60% QWOT±10%, 40% harmonic multiples (λ/8, λ/2) with ±5nm noise injection in first optimization step
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (under 30-layer limit)
All thicknesses should remain in manufacturable range 40-350nm
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporated/sputtered coating materials
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength through constructive interference of reflected waves from each interface
Recalled knowledge: High/low index contrast (HfO2 n≈2.0, SiO2 n≈1.45 at visible wavelengths) determines reflectance bandwidth and peak value
Recalled knowledge: Gradient-based thickness optimization can converge to local minima when starting from symmetric initial conditions
Recalled knowledge: Harmonic thickness perturbations (half-wave, quarter-wave multiples) maintain physical meaning while breaking optimizer symmetry
Recalled knowledge: Dichroic filters for quantum applications typically prioritize transmission in signal band over reflection in blocking band
expected_advantages: Hybrid initialization should escape the 130nm attractor basin observed in prior iterations
40% harmonic candidates may discover thickness combinations that pure QWOT initialization cannot reach
Noise injection prevents exact symmetry that causes gradient cancellation
Should improve best_target_score from prior 0.868-0.934 range while maintaining robustness
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 extinction coefficient is negligible at 1530-1565nm - would need to check material dataset for k values
Uncertain optimal center wavelength for QWOT calculation (550nm vs 600nm for visible blocking) - this choice affects all baseline thicknesses
Recalled refractive indices are approximate: HfO2 n≈1.9-2.1, SiO2 n≈1.45-1.48 depending on deposition method and wavelength
Harmonic initialization may produce some candidates with thicknesses outside manufacturable range (<40nm or >350nm)
Did not verify whether 24 layers is optimal vs 20 or 28 layers - fixed by prior iteration convention
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer materials alternate HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with HfO2 at the air interface. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700nm band. Use hybrid initialization: 60% of candidates start from quarter-wave optical thickness (center wavelength 550nm) with ±10% perturbation, 40% start from harmonic multiples (λ/8 and λ/2 optical thicknesses) with ±5nm random noise injection in the first optimization step. All thicknesses must remain between 40nm and 350nm. Total layer count is exactly 24. Materials are hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for each round.
routes.revision_reason: Hybrid initialization scheme per feedback directive: replacing strict QWOT-centered Gaussian with 60% QWOT±10% plus 40% harmonic half/double multiples with ±5nm noise injection to escape local minima observed in prior iterations

Whether HfO2 has measurable extinction at 1530-1565nm that would affect transmission - material dataset k values not checked
Whether 24 layers is the optimal count vs 20, 22, 26, or 28 - fixed by prior iteration convention rather than systematic comparison
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all routes fail to achieve best_target_score > 0.85 with tightest_margin > 0.4 after 5 rounds, reconsider whether the material pair (HfO2/SiO2) can physically satisfy both spectral requirements with only 24 layers, or whether the layer count limit needs revision

expected_observations: If hybrid initialization hypothesis holds: best_target_score should rise or remain stable across rounds while tightest_margin does not fall below 0.4
If hybrid initialization fails to improve convergence: best_target_score should plateau earlier than prior iterations and valid_candidates may decrease
Thicknesses_nm should show greater variance in the 40% harmonic-initialized candidates compared to QWOT-centered candidates
Run_status should remain completed with physically_valid_candidate_count >= 5 per round
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds from 40-350nm to 30-400nm and continue
If tightest_margin falls below 0.3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce noise injection amplitude from ±5nm to ±2nm and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
